ordered_diagnoses: Muscle weakness due to chronic disease

facts.raw_span: 87-year-old Cantonese-speaking man
Alzheimer’s dementia, hypertension, stroke, hyperlipidaemia, gout, peptic ulcer, and chronic kidney disease
one week of increasing left leg pain and weakness
impaired mobility
a single episode of urinary incontinence
anorexia and a 12% body-weight loss over six months
blood pressure was 88/45 mmHg
heart rate 96/min
elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 76 mg/L, WCC 11.9 × 10^9/L, neutrophils 8.5 × 10^9/L)
pre-renal acute-on-chronic kidney injury
bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement and a left-sided insertional tendinopathy
no evidence of trochanteric bursitis

concepts.why: The patient presents with left leg pain and weakness, elevated inflammatory markers, and an MRI showing bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement and a left-sided insertional tendinopathy.
The patient has a history of chronic kidney disease and presents with pre-renal acute-on-chronic kidney injury.
The patient's blood pressure is 88/45 mmHg, which is lower than normal.
The patient has a history of gout, which could be contributing to his current symptoms.
The patient presents with elevated inflammatory markers, which could be indicative of sepsis.
